chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Saif from his brother from his father from 'Asim from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'One who restrains himself from the honor/privileges of people, Allah will restrain His punishment from him on the Day of Judgment; and one who restrains his anger from people, Allah will excuse him (release him from his sins) on the Day of Judgment.'

key_terms.أَعْرَاضِ: Honor, privileges, or what is sacred to people (plural of 'irad)
key_terms.أَقَالَهُ: He excused him / released him (from sins)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for controlling anger and guarding people's honor according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) links the social virtue of *kaff al-awra* (withholding one's gaze and faults) to divine protection from the punishment of the Hereafter. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *ghidhb* (anger management) not merely as personal discipline, but as a mechanism for *'afw* (divine pardon), reflecting the broader theological principle that interpersonal ethics directly influence one's spiritual standing before Allah.
